paper_title: MICROSCOPE mission: first constraints on the violation of the weak equivalence principle by a light scalar dilaton
coupling_convention: dimensionless Yukawa strength |alpha| relative to gravity for a scalar coupled to baryon number B (alpha = alpha_i*alpha_j with q=B charge normalization, as in Eq. 5 of paper); NOT converted to g_B
notes: MICROSCOPE first WEP results (Eotvos parameter eta=(-1+-27)e-15 at 2-sigma) used to constrain a light scalar dilaton. Paper reports multiple couplings: |alpha|<1e-11 for coupling to baryon number B (extracted here as ScalarBaryon per hint), |alpha|<1e-12 for coupling to B-L (could alternatively be extracted as VectorBL), and |d_e|<1e-4 for a dilaton coupled only to the EM sector (ScalarPhoton) valid for 1e-18<m<1e-11 eV. The baryon-coupling bound is quoted as mass-independent for m_phi < 1e-12 eV (range > few 1e5 m); encoded as a flat two-point line spanning 1e-18 to 1e-12 eV (constraint saturates/extends to the massless limit at low mass, lower endpoint chosen to match the paper's stated d_e validity floor). Full exclusion curves are only shown in figures (Figs. 1-2), not tabulated; the flat value is the plateau quoted in text/abstract.
